clue.text: Excess force in confident appeal

indicators.note: one thing set in another sits inside it, so the force letter goes within the word for confident

blocks.note: confident means certain
F is the physics symbol for force
'it' is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Someone appealing with far too much forceful confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: SUR(F)E then IT. 'It' meaning sex appeal comes from the 1920s film star Clara Bow, the It girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A surfeit is an overabundance, a quantity well beyond what is needed.

clue.text: Spectacle involving skill coming up directly

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means read from bottom to top, so the word for skill goes backwards
involving means taking in, so the word for spectacle holds the other piece

blocks.note: a spectacle is a sight
art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A display of talent rising straight upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight as an adverb means at once or without detour, as in 'go straight home'.

clue.text: Spy hoard, stirred to make expression of ecstasy

indicators.note: stirred means mixed up, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A secret agent thrilled at finding a stash of treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhapsody is an effusively enthusiastic outpouring of feeling in speech or writing.

clue.text: Praise text, old-fashioned to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent means partly, so only part of the following words is used

blocks.note: found running across the two words

explanation.surface: Admiring a piece of writing that is a bit dated.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to laud or glorify enthusiastically.

clue.text: Novel gag, hasty, better after revision

indicators.note: a revision reworks material, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: An editor improving a rushed joke in a book draft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective for a new gag, but it is the definition: a book.
explanation.definitionFit: F. Scott Fitzgerald's 1925 book about Jay Gatsby is a classic American work of fiction.

clue.text: Answer following reasonable concern

blocks.note: A is the usual abbreviation for answer
f. is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
reasonable means fair or just

explanation.surface: An answer that follows from a sensible worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' looks like a positional instruction, but it is the abbreviation F, as in 'pp. 10 ff.'
explanation.definitionFit: An affair is a matter or business, something that is one's concern, as in 'that's my affair'.

clue.text: In favour of effort, study taboo

blocks.note: for means supporting
a bid is an attempt or effort
a den is a private study room

explanation.surface: Supporting hard work while studying something off-limits.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taboo is prohibited by custom, not allowed.

clue.text: Sour account about police department on island

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the police abbreviation is read backwards
on here means placed next after, so the police piece follows the island rather than preceding it

blocks.note: AC is the abbreviation for account
I is the abbreviation for island
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: A bitter report concerning the island's police force.
explanation.walkthrough: CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, is the British plain-clothes detective branch; 'about' looks like 'concerning' but turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidic means sharp-tasting or tart, like vinegar or lemon juice.

clue.text: Extend contract or quit

blocks.note: first meaning: put one's name to an agreement again
second meaning: give up a job

explanation.surface: A footballer weighing up staying on or walking away.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as RE-SIGN it means sign again; as one word it means leave a post. The two senses are opposites.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-signing renews an agreement, while resigning formally gives up a position of employment.

clue.text: Supply officers in region on planet disrupted by alien's rising

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the alien's letters go backwards
something disrupted has another thing break into it, so the planet is split open around the other piece

blocks.note: a quarter is a district or region of a town
the red planet
ET is the film alien, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: Military supply staff on a planet thrown into chaos by an alien uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Quartermasters are army officers responsible for provisions, equipment and accommodation.

clue.text: Be uncomfortably hot while in bunk

indicators.note: placed in something means placed within it, so the word for while goes inside the word for bunk

blocks.note: bunk is nonsense, as is rot
while and as both mean during the time that

explanation.surface: Sweltering in a bunk bed at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunk' suggests a bed, but here it means nonsense: RO(AS)T.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast informally means to feel extremely warm, as on a sweltering summer day.

clue.text: Royal attendants echo doubts about king

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for doubts wraps round the king

blocks.note: Echo is E in the NATO phonetic alphabet
doubts raised are queries
R is for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Courtiers repeating their misgivings about the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Equerries are officers of the British royal household who personally attend members of the royal family.

clue.text: Narrow-minded snub, ignoring conclusion by revolutionary artist

indicators.note: ignoring the conclusion means leaving off the final letter of the word for snub
a revolution turns something round, so the abbreviation for artist is read backwards

blocks.note: to snub someone is to slight or insult them
RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A provincial snub delivered by a radical painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snub' looks like the definition beside narrow-minded, but it supplies a longer word for a slight, which then loses its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Insular describes someone cut off and uninterested in outside ideas, like an isolated island, hence parochial.

clue.text: Barrier formed by river, not well

blocks.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
someone not well is ailing or sick

explanation.surface: A fence made from a river and an unwell person, oddly.
explanation.definitionFit: A railing is a fence of upright bars, which serves to block or enclose.

clue.text: Engine dad had designed for secret purpose

indicators.note: something designed is drawn up afresh, so these letters are laid out in a new plan

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Father built a machine with some ulterior motive.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden agenda is a concealed motive or plan behind an apparently innocent action.

clue.text: Involved in goal, securing team's first corner

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of team
securing means holding fast, so the word for goal encloses the rest

blocks.note: an end is an aim or goal
opening letter of team
a corner is an angle

explanation.surface: A footballer caught up in a goal from a corner kick.
explanation.walkthrough: EN(T + ANGLE)D. 'Goal' suggests football but means aim.
explanation.definitionFit: Entangled means caught up or embroiled in a situation, just as being involved implies.

clue.text: Upset about soldier with angry speech lacking knowledge

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the first two pieces are read upwards

blocks.note: on means concerning
a GI is an American soldier
a rant is an angry tirade

explanation.surface: An angry soldier's tirade showing he knows nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorant means uninformed, without education or awareness of something.

clue.text: Unravelling lies, ends inactivity

indicators.note: unravelling pulls apart what was knitted, so these letters come loose and are rearranged

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Once the deceit unravels, the loafing stops.
explanation.definitionFit: Idleness is the state of doing nothing, of laziness or being unoccupied.

clue.text: Carefully controlled step by chap getting on

blocks.note: a step in a process is a stage
a chap is a man
getting on means growing old

explanation.surface: An elderly man being guided step by step.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage-managed events are arranged and orchestrated behind the scenes for effect, like a theatrical production.

clue.text: Principles one compromises?

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
compromises are agreements or deals

explanation.surface: Does someone trade away their principles?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the irony: principles are exactly what one compromises in a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are standards of perfection or moral values that a person tries to live by.

clue.text: Erase error initially supported by very loud expert

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of error

blocks.note: opening letter of error
ff is fortissimo in musical notation
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: Rubbing out a mistake, backed by a loud specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supported by' puts the error letter above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To efface is to wipe out or rub away, so that no mark remains.

clue.text: No longer working in December, time filled with merriment

indicators.note: something filled with merriment has it inside, so the date abbreviation with time holds the next word

blocks.note: DEC is the calendar abbreviation
T is the abbreviation for time
merriment is fun

explanation.surface: Christmas fun in December when nobody is at work.
explanation.walkthrough: The month and time abbreviations sit side by side, and the merriment is tucked between the month's second and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Defunct describes a machine or organisation that has ceased to operate or exist.

clue.text: Fancy duck followed by seconds in endless meal

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the meal word is cut off
placed in the meal means set inside its letters

blocks.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, shaped like O
S is the abbreviation for seconds
supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: Fancy roast duck with second helpings at a never-ending dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: SUPPE(r) holds O and S: SUPP(OS)E. 'Fancy' looks like an adjective for the duck but is a verb meaning imagine.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy, in the sense of imagine or think, is to suppose something is so.

clue.text: Assistant for each essay

blocks.note: a PA is a personal assistant
per means for each, as in miles per hour

explanation.surface: An assistant assigned to every essay.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper is a written composition or academic article on a subject.

clue.text: Free article, almost useless, with large fit

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word for useless loses its last letter

blocks.note: a is the indefinite article
vain means futile or useless
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
fit to do something is able

explanation.surface: A useless large garment offered free.
explanation.walkthrough: A + VAI(n) + L + ABLE. 'Fit' looks like the size of clothing but means capable.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone free is not otherwise engaged and so can be called on; something free can be had.

clue.text: Tree without decoration by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it tells us to go by how the word for undecorated is pronounced

blocks.note: plain means unadorned

explanation.surface: A tree stripped bare of ornament, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: The plane is a broad-leaved tree common in city streets, especially the London plane.

clue.text: Dates, not normally variable, fixed

indicators.note: not in the normal way means not in the normal order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
y is a standard algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Appointments that are usually changeable are now set firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variable' sits beside 'fixed' as if they were opposites in the surface, but it supplies a single algebra letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady means firmly placed and stable, not moving or wobbling.

clue.text: Cloud level about right

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for level wraps round the abbreviation for right

blocks.note: a level in a hierarchy is a status
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Cloud height being about right.
explanation.walkthrough: ST(R)ATUS. 'Level' looks like an altitude for the cloud but means standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Stratus is a low, grey, layered formation that forms a uniform sheet across the sky.
